text:
**Short answer:** You need about 300–350 W of solar to fully recharge a 1,000 Wh power station in one sunny day. A 200 W panel will do it in about 1.5 days.

**The math** (both guides use the same formula):
- Daily energy = panel watts × peak sun hours × about 0.7–0.75. The 0.7–0.75 factor covers real-world losses from heat, panel angle, dust, cables, and charge-controller conversion.
- For a one-day refill, panel watts = 1,000 ÷ (peak sun hours × 0.75).

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a 1-day refill |
|---|---|
| 3 | about 450 W |
| 4 | about 340 W |
| 5 | about 270 W |

Peak sun hours means hours of full-strength sun, not daylight hours. In the continental US that's typically 4–6 in summer and 2–4 in winter or cloudy weather.

**If you don't need a one-day refill:** A common rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5, which gives 200 W. At about 4–4.5 peak sun hours, that fills the station in roughly 1.5 days ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Check your station's limits before buying:**
- **Maximum solar input watts:** The station won't accept more than this, so extra panel watts are wasted.
- **Voltage range:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (VOC) must stay within what the station accepts. Going over can damage it.
- **Connector type:** MC4, XT60, and DC barrel are common. You may need an adapter cable.

**A panel that fits this range:** The ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel is listed at $299. With code ALLPOWERS26, the price is $269.10 ([deal listing](https://dealectric.com/lab/V1/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel), [buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel)). I haven't verified its specs against your station. Confirm that your station's input limit and voltage range can take 400 W.

If you tell me which power station you have and roughly where you'll use it, I can narrow this to a specific panel size.

Sources: [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)
